subject: DPA negotiation: SCC addendum, subprocessors, and e-sign plan
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@finservco.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@finservco.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Draft DPA + SCCs and execution preferences

Hi Stephanie / Markus,

Attached is FinServCo's redline of your standard DPA along with our proposed EU SCC addendum. Our main open points are:

- Breach notification timing: we prefer 48 hours for initial notification of a confirmed unauthorized disclosure, with substantive updates every 7 calendar days.
- Subprocessor commitments: we need a 30-day notification window and the ability to object to new subprocessors where the objection can be escalated to a neutral arbiter.
- For EU data leaving jurisdiction we expect SCCs + a short addendum stating parties will cooperate on regulator requests.

We can execute via DocuSign — please indicate who at Redwood will initiate the envelope and whether you can produce the current subprocessor registry as a CSV.

I'll also need to confirm what forensic artifacts you can provide during an investigation (e.g., access logs, KV cache records, audit logs) and whether SOC2 reports are available on request.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
Senior Counsel, FinServCo

Attachments: FinServCo_DPA_redline.docx, SCCs_EU_Addendum.pdf, subprocessors_list_request.txt

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft DPA + SCCs and execution preferences

Markus / Neha — forwarding FinServCo's redline. High level takeaways and recommended playbook: 

- Breach timing: Redwood default is 72 hours for initial notification after discovery unless constrained by law. Recommend we push for 72h initial notification with commitment to notify regulators as required by law and provide interim updates at 3, 10, 30 days (or sooner).
- Subprocessors: we already publish a registry; suggest we propose a 10-business-day objection window (shorter than their 30) and add objective grounds for objection (e.g., data residency or security posture).
- SCCs / Transfers: propose SCCs + EU Addendum paragraph; confirm we can provide SCC annex and follow-the-sun cooperation for regulator requests.
- Evidence: we can provide logs and forensics subject to data minimization and legal protections; Neha, can you confirm what exact artifacts we can safely hand over and timing?

Execution: prefer DocuSign. Laura — can your team own the envelope and signer sequence (Redwood signs first -> FinServCo countersigns)? If procurement prefers countersign, we can adapt. Goal: get executed within 7 business days once language is agreed.

I attached a short checklist I want us to propose back: 72h initial notice, incident cooperation clause, SCC addendum, subprocessors registry link, and DocuSign envelope plan.

-Steph

Attachments: internal_dpa_playbook.txt

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft DPA + SCCs and execution preferences

Thanks — drafting counter language below (feel free to copy into a redline):

1) Breach notification. Proposed clause: "Supplier will notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours after Supplier becomes aware of a confirmed security incident resulting in unauthorized access to Customer Personal Data. Supplier will include in the notification (to the extent known at the time) a summary of the nature of the incident, the categories of Personal Data affected, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to be taken. Supplier will provide regular written updates to Customer at reasonably agreed intervals during the investigation and will cooperate to support Customer's regulatory obligations."

2) Interim updates cadence: propose "initial notification within 72 hours, substantive updates as available and at minimum at 3, 10 and 30 calendar days, or until closed."

3) Subprocessors: "Supplier will publish and maintain a current list of subprocessors. Supplier will notify Customer of any new subprocessor at least ten (10) business days in advance and Customer may object on reasonable grounds related to data protection; the parties will use good faith efforts to resolve objections, and, if not resolved within ten (10) business days, either party may refer the dispute to escalation (in writing) followed by a neutral third-party review."

4) Transfers / SCCs: "Where SCCs are required, Supplier shall execute the standard EU SCCs and include an addendum ensuring cooperation on regulator requests and timely provision of supporting documentation. For UK transfers, the parties will execute the UK Addendum where applicable."

5) Evidence scope: "Supplier will make available relevant logs and forensic output subject to legal and privacy constraints; Supplier will not provide production-level access or unrelated customer data; requests for large datasets will be handled under a separate data access process and may require a protective order."

Neha — please confirm we can commit to the 72h window and what forensic artifacts are available (access logs, audit trail, container IDs, KV cache timestamps).

If everyone is good, I can integrate into a redline and send back to FinServCo.

-Markus

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@finservco.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@finservco.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs and execution preferences

Thanks Markus — that language mostly addresses our concerns. A few clarifications before we proceed to a joint redline: 

- 72 hours is acceptable as long as it's "after Supplier becomes aware" rather than "after discovery" — please ensure the wording is precise.
- For the subprocessor objection and neutral review: can you specify the identity/selection process for the neutral reviewer (e.g., an independent security counsel or an industry arbitration service)?
- Evidence scope: we need to confirm whether you can provide: (a) raw access logs for the affected tenant for a 90-day window, and (b) a CSV export of user activity relevant to the incident. If those require a court order or protective order, please flag now.

Execution: we prefer Redwood to initiate DocuSign and set the signing order so FinServCo countersigns last. Please include who will be the envelope owner and the email to expect. Once we have the joint redline we will route through procurement for signature.

Best,
Emma

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@finservco.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, docusign_ops@docusign.com
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs and execution preferences

Emma — thanks for the quick review. Agreed on the "becomes aware" phrasing; we'll ensure that's explicit. On the neutral reviewer: propose we suggest "an independent security counsel agreed by the parties or, failing agreement, an industry arbitration service such as JAMS or LCIA". Open to suggestions from your side.

Neha confirms we can provide tenant-scoped access logs and activity exports for a 90-day window; large raw data extracts will require a protective order or separate agreement. We will include a short forensic evidence annex specifying delivery timelines and redaction/minimization commitments.

Laura will own the DocuSign envelope. Laura — can your team create the DocuSign envelope with Redwood as the first signer and FinServCo as final signer? If yes, please initiate once we exchange the final redline. Emma — you should expect an envelope from contracts@redwood.com (Laura's team).

Plan: Markus to produce joint redline by EOD Tue, internal review Wed, send to FinServCo Wed afternoon; target execution within 7 business days after mutual redline.

Thanks,
-Steph

Attachments: subprocessors_list_20260601.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@finservco.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: docusign_ops@docusign.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Executed DPA and envelope confirmation

Hi all — quick update: I initiated the envelope from contracts@redwood.com this morning (DocuSign envelope id 12345). Redwood signed first; FinServCo countersigned at 13:05 ET. Attached is the executed PDF and the DocuSign confirmation.

Summary of agreed points incorporated into the final executed DPA:
- Initial notification: Supplier will notify Customer within seventy-two (72) hours after Supplier becomes aware of a confirmed security incident impacting Customer Personal Data.
- Interim updates at approximately 3, 10 and 30 days and as available.
- Subprocessor notifications: 10 business day notice; Customer may object on reasonable grounds. Disputes to be escalated and, if unresolved, referred to independent reviewer.
- Transfers: execution of EU SCCs with an addendum for regulator cooperation; UK Addendum where applicable.
- Evidence: tenant-scoped logs and CSV exports for a 90-day window; large raw datasets require protective order.

Attachments: FinServCo_Signed_DPA.pdf, DocuSign_envelope_12345.pdf

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
